review: Agent user journey and layout discovery
coordinator_reproductions: Shape text "2. ..." written as auto-numbered paragraph (renders "1.")
generate exits 0 for chart type stacked-bar with a placeholder image

delights.title: deck_id + patch makes repair nearly free
Semantic validation errors are exact and one-step fixable
Speed: the whole loop is sub-second apart from thumbnails
Copy-ready examples: zero unknown-field errors while authoring, first render wrote a real deck
Pixel content hashes make the review protocol honest and cheap
Good defaults without asking: highlighted final bar and data labels, takeaway band, source line, date footer and page numbers
Refuses to shrink text below 12pt instead of shipping unreadable slides, and names the field
list_templates compact is small and useful
Chart and diagram candidates come with a data_contract and a next_tool_call that runs verbatim
Semantic kinds for org, 8 quotes, option matrix, funnel+insights and regions were valid on the first attempt and looked right
`regions` kind: chart + stat + timeline in one slide from ~15 lines
Render-time unknown-key errors name the key, why it matters and the accepted keys
show_pattern is an authoritative contract: closed schema, min/max items, per-count character budgets, example_values
validate_pattern answers a wrong key with did_you_mean, a patch and a pointer to show_pattern
Single-slide render loop is fast and returns a real image
Capacity strings on candidates ('3-8', 'objective + 3-5 pillars + foundation') and limits in kind summaries let me check item counts before authoring
journey-maturity-model 'We are here' marker and value-chain highlight render exactly as intended
deck_id + patch makes repair rounds tiny and tells me what to re-inspect
Every validate finding carries a path into my spec, and dropped content is called out as DROPPED
Chart series/category mismatch caught before render with exact counts
Title, source and closing fixes worked first time; meta.source cleared four findings with one op
Thumbnails -> review hand-off is prefilled and the review was accepted first try
Fast: validate <0.25s, render 0.3-0.45s, 12 thumbnails ~2s
Same spec rendered on midnight-blue and p-style with no layout breakage
describe_finding for PATTERN_DEGRADED explains from/to/reason and says content is never lost
First DeckSpec was valid on the first try and rendered a good 7-slide deck in 0.3 s; thumbnails took 3 s
Schema descriptions state counts, character budgets and degradation behaviour per kind; `semantic explain` shows the chosen pattern, layout and alternatives per slide
Errors are specific, list everything in one pass and suggest the fix
Templates are embedded, so the CLI works with no --templates-dir
Output is deterministic and stdout JSON is never mixed with log lines
Placeholder copy is caught (WEAK_CONTENT) and capabilities carries a correct MCP-to-CLI mapping; top-level help lists MCP-only tools with CLI workarounds
deck_id + patch held state across 30+ calls; a whole-deck template switch was one 169-byte call
changed_slides + next_tool_call with slide_indices prefilled: one changed slide re-inspected in about 1.5 s and 37 KB instead of 268 KB
Patch errors are precise, and the patch is atomic
Unknown arguments are rejected with the accepted list rather than ignored
First render succeeded on the first attempt from catalog examples; turns 1, 4, 5, 6 and 8 each rendered on their first call
Thumbnails are content-addressed and cached: an old revision's slide came back in 0.01 s and its hash proved the title slide had not changed
Appendix handling just worked: section with appendix:true is unnumbered and the slide after it is paged 'A1'; notes landed in all ten notes slides
The slide list (index, kind, title) in every render response is a cheap way to confirm what sits at each index after a structural patch
submit_visual_review verified all ten image hashes against the server's own render in one call
Switching template surfaced template-specific findings with a ready patch

findings.title: Installed skill contradicts the binary and nothing tells the agent it is stale
Default-profile responses point agents at tools and documents they cannot reach
An agent reads about 23k tokens before it can author anything; the full profile costs 335 KB
A kind's item_schema is 6-37 KB because every alias is expanded as its own property
Named-pattern recommendations give no data shape, example or next step in the default profile
recommend_visual ranks the wrong visual first for plain intents
recommend_visual answers in raw vocabulary and never recommends a DeckSpec kind
An agent cannot see a layout before authoring it
One visual has up to three names and three data shapes
plan_deck drops parts of the brief while reporting unplaced_facts: []
plan_deck spends the slide budget on an agenda and dividers without saying so
The CLI has no kind catalogue: DeckSpec discovery is a 172 KB schema without examples
CLI template and icon discovery returns 84 KB to 738 KB with no way to ask for names only
house_diagram advertises `floors` but silently drops content either way
Shape text that starts with "2." is rendered as "1."
Readability refusals blame the author for text the engine wrote
Text budgets are missing from the catalogue and differ by template, so fit is learned by failing
A recommendation that spans two options cannot be expressed
A screenshot with callouts pointing at parts of it cannot be authored in DeckSpec
Swimlane arrows follow column order, and the idiom that makes them right is only in one example
A timeline with end dates draws identical full-width bars and still scores 100
validate_deck_spec says "no issues" for raw pattern and diagram payloads that render then refuses
Validation runs without the render template, so its verdict differs from the render
validate and render report different finding sets for the same stored deck
Severity does not say whether a finding blocks: info and warning findings stop the render gate
The storyline gate cannot be waived when the user asked for a deck shape that breaks it
Findings arrive in tiers and one item at a time, so a flawed draft takes seven validates
Machine-suggested patches do not always clear the finding they come with
Repair advice names controls the caller's surface does not have
Fit diagnostics name the wrong text and the wrong constraint
One root cause produces many findings and large responses
Slides are addressed in five notations with mixed index bases
Unknown kinds and keys get uneven help, and their side effects are reported as separate causes
Splitting a table as advised triggers a monotony finding, and a section divider can sit between the halves
Placeholder copy passes the deterministic gate
score_deck gives 100 and passes the gate on slides that are visibly weak
Option matrix column headers render at two font sizes
A KPI card with a two-line label sits higher than its neighbours
The table highlight column renders blue on the forest-green template
KPIs in a short region draw the number over its label with only an info finding
Slides have no stable handle; every address is an index that shifts
No move or copy operation and no way to read back the stored spec
changed_slides is a positional diff: shifted and notes-only slides look edited
No way to find a fact across the deck
No revision history, undo or fork for a deck handle
A patch is stored even when its render fails, and the response does not say so
Every patch render returns 7-9.5 KB, most of it unchanged summaries
A notes-only edit changes the 50-dpi thumbnail hash of unrelated slides
The CLI cannot write slide PNGs; images arrive only as base64 inside JSON
Raw validate and generate report success for a deck whose chart cannot render
CLI flags mean different things in different subcommands, and help exits 1
CLI output is noisy and inconsistent: repeated log lines, two JSON shapes, wrong subcommand name
Renders leave sidecars and hundreds of megabytes of temp files behind
A spec that is clean on one template is refused on another, and nothing checks portability up front
Templates that uppercase titles change the meaning of units
submit_visual_review does not say which severities and categories it accepts
An agenda without a title raises MISSING_TITLE with no path although the title is optional
No repeatable check that the agent journey stays good

limits: Five agent journeys on one machine and one day; enjoyment scores are self-reported by the agents; root causes were not investigated in code unless a bead says so.
